stumbles.quote: Round 1 measured only that configuration and concluded that domain vocabulary does not help much. Round 2 traced the small saving to the pre-tokenizer, and that conclusion no longer holds.
stumbles.why: Rounds 1 and 2 are never introduced; a first-time reader doesn't know what earlier experiment or version these refer to.

stumbles.quote: Ettin's tokenizer spends 376 tokens per abstract.
stumbles.why: Unclear whether this is the baseline on the 2,000 held-out abstracts, and the retrained figure is never stated, so the 21% can't be checked.

stumbles.quote: Oskar asked on 2026-11-06 whether "we [could] create an entirely custom domain Ettin model with custom token table ... for life sciences".
stumbles.why: Oskar is unexplained, and the quote is elided and bracketed, so the question's context is unclear.

stumbles.quote: The follow-up experiment, lifesci-ettin, trains models on the new table, and this experiment does not cover it.
stumbles.why: Ambiguous: it is unclear whether lifesci-ettin exists yet or is only planned, and "trains" reads as if it is done.

stumbles.quote: This experiment answers the tokenizer half of that question.
stumbles.why: The other half is only implied to be model training, and "cheaper" is taken to mean fewer tokens, never stated as cost in compute or money.

point: A 50K BPE retrained on PubMed abstracts with whitespace-only pre-tokenization cuts tokens by 21% versus Ettin's tokenizer, but keeping the GPT-2 pre-tokenizer cuts only 8%, so the pre-tokenizer matters as much as the vocabulary.
